the cassette is ever re-cut with a different 3′ boundary, the filter position must move with it; the
constant lives in `scripts/slurm/analysis/integration-sites.sh`.

**Detection is read-through-limited, so absence is weak evidence.** A cell is labelled only if one of
its few read-through molecules happened to be captured and sequenced. Most cells in a real clone carry
no label. Clone *sizes* here are therefore samples, not counts, and comparing them across tubes
assumes comparable depth.

**Small sites sit near the background, and the wild-type tubes do not bound all of it.** A wild-type
tube bounds *cross-tube* error — index hopping and carry-over — and nothing else. It cannot bound
within-tube ambient, where every lysed mCherry⁺ cell sheds vector RNA into the shared soup. That is
measured separately from sub-threshold droplets, computed each run across both channels:

```{r ambient}
readr::read_csv(file.path(sites_dir, "ambient_rate.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(junction_barcodes >= 10) |>
  dplyr::transmute(tube, `junction-bearing barcodes` = junction_barcodes,
                   `of those, a called cell` = in_called_cells,
                   `not a cell` = not_cells,
                   `ambient share` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * ambient_share),
                   `rate per called cell` = sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * rate_per_cell),
                   `rate per empty droplet` = sprintf("%.1e", rate_per_empty),
                   `ratio` = scales::comma(round(ratio))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The comparison that makes the number mean something is the last column: a junction in one of 2.5
million empty droplets and a junction in one of 20,000 cells are different events, and per droplet
the signal is three to four orders of magnitude stronger in cells. These are also exactly the
barcodes the called-cell filter removes from the cell table — the filter is applied where cells are
counted and **not** to the clip and genomic tables, because this measurement is computed from the
rows it removes.

Folding in the genome-mapped channel was a check on this in its own right: it raised the
junction-bearing barcode count substantially and left the non-cell count unchanged. The new channel
added signal without adding ambient, which is what should happen if the extra reads are real
junctions rather than background — a doubling of a background-driven signal would have doubled its
background with it. Scaled by the depth difference between a cell and an empty droplet — the one
multiplier not measured here — this is of order 1–2% of labelled cells, consistent with the doublet
rate. Scaled by the depth difference between a cell and an empty droplet — the one multiplier not
measured here — that is of order 1–2% of labelled cells, consistent with the doublet rate.

The assignment tier's own error rate is now measured rather than argued, by **decoy flanks**: 100
flanks cut from random matched positions and carried through the identical positional test. They
return zero hits at every clip length from 10 bp up, which also audits the anchoring, since a decoy
has no junction and any hit passing it would mean the test is mis-implemented. Below 10 bp they
return 2, which is what set `min_assign`.

**The genome-mapped channel needed its own decoy, and it is a different decoy.** The flank decoys
bound assignment and say nothing about the channel that now calls four sites on its own and carries
IS10's 99 cells. That channel's claim is narrower: a read the aligner placed at MAPQ 255, whose
soft-clipped end matches the last 13 bases of the provirus terminus within the absorption window, is
a junction read. `genomic_decoy_rate()` tests how often that is true of a terminus that cannot be
there — the same 13 bases **permuted to the same composition**, which matters, because the real
13-mer `AAAATCTCTAGCA` carries six adenines and a permutation of the whole 18-base terminus leaves
only three. A-rich *k*-mers are commoner in a mammalian genome, so a composition-mismatched decoy
understates the rate in the direction that flatters the channel.

On chr19 in Rx_4 — 27.6M alignments, a slice that contains a real site with 29 reads —
`CCTACAAAGTTAA` returns **zero hits**. Nothing else on that chromosome in that tube looks like a
junction once the terminus is scrambled. Stated as a bound rather than as a zero: 0 observed puts a
95% Poisson ceiling of 3 events on that slice, against 29 real.

**The genome-wide pass has now run** (job 35768797, 2 h 00 m, all eight tubes), and the answer is
not zero:

| tube | Rx_1 | Rx_2 | Rx_3 | Rx_4 | Rx_5 | Rx_6 | Rx_7 | Rx_8 | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| real reads | 0 | 12 | 47 | 800 | 1 | 537 | 25 | 0 | **1,422** |
| decoy reads | 0 | 2 | 3 | 1 | 0 | 4 | 0 | 5 | **15** |
| decoy positions | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 2 | 9 |

**1.1% of reads, and no callable site.** The 15 decoy reads scatter over 7 positions across 8 tubes —
at most a few reads at any one of them — while the 1,422 real reads concentrate at 47 positions, 800
of them at 16 positions in Rx_4 alone. A site needs `min_cells` distinct cells and `min_umis`
molecules at one base, and nothing in the decoy output approaches that. So the error rate to quote is
**1.1% at the read level and zero at the site level**, which is the level the site list is built at.

Two details worth keeping. **Rx_8 is the sharpest result in the table**: a wild-type tube, zero real
reads, and 5 decoy reads — so in material with no provirus at all, the real 13-mer finds nothing and
a composition-matched random one finds five. The real terminus is not merely better than chance here,
it is cleanly separated from it. And at the cell level 1.1% of 1,396 folded-in reads is roughly 15
reads, so of the labelled cells perhaps 15 could carry a spurious label — the same order as the
ambient and doublet rates, and not concentrated anywhere.

One limitation of this run, for whoever tightens it: `genomic_decoy_rate()` stores counts per tube,
not cells per decoy position, so "no callable site" is inferred from reads-per-position rather than
measured against the floor directly. That is the next thing to add if the bound ever needs to be
airtight.

It is a separate job rather than a stage of the main one because it costs what the genomic scan
costs, and a control must not sit on the critical path of a run someone is waiting for. It reads the
real counts from the genomic stage's cache instead of rescanning for them, which is the difference
between ~1 h 50 m and ~3 h 30 m.

The cell and UMI floor was the one genuinely arbitrary parameter in the chain, and it is now measured
rather than asserted — gain against loss at every value, with vector transcript as the quality axis
(*What the floor admits, and what it turns away*). Rule C′ still gives a sub-floor cluster one
principled route back in, on a strand-matched target-site duplication, but at the relaxed floor it
**promotes nothing**: chrX:100,691,113 now clears the floor on its own. The rule stands with zero
current effect, which is the right state for a safeguard.

**Per-clone detection is not uniform, so λ differs by site** — and this is the covariate the
completeness section now regresses λ on, in place of one imputed median. Vector expression per cell
spans about sevenfold across clones — median UMIs on the reporter contig run from 1 at IS03 and 3 at IS04 to 6 at
IS02 and 7 at IS05, with IS04 at roughly half of IS01 and IS02 combined (Wilcoxon *p* = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵).
This is direct evidence that position effects operate at these loci, and it means a per-site
detection rate assumed constant is misspecified — which matters for every clone-size statement.
Separately, read-through termination is multi-site: the vector-portion length distribution at IS02
shows at least three over-represented positions at molecule level (reads per UMI is flat at ~1.5
across it), so a λ built on a single termination site is also misspecified.

**Leakage into the mCherry⁻ tubes was reported here as animal-structured. On the proper
denominator it is not, and the correction is instructive.** The figures were B0304 14.0% of its
labelled cells in the mCherry⁻ tubes, against 3.6% for B0301 and 0.2% for B0303 — a seventy-fold
spread. Those numbers are arithmetically correct and they measure the wrong thing: they are the
*composition* of each mouse's labelled cells, and composition follows where that mouse's cells were
sorted.

```{r leakage-rates}
# Per-mouse, per-sort-fraction cell counts, from the hashtag call. The denominator is the only thing
# that makes the labelled counts comparable, and it is the quantity the metadata queries asked for.
sort_of <- function(tb) ifelse(tb %in% c("Rx_4", "Rx_6"), "mCherry+", "mCherry−")
mouse_cells <- embedding |>
  dplyr::filter(tube %in% c("Rx_3", "Rx_4", "Rx_6", "Rx_7"),
                grepl("^TotalSeq-B03", as.character(replicate))) |>
  dplyr::transmute(cell, tube, mouse = sub("^TotalSeq-", "", replicate), sort = sort_of(tube))

dplyr::left_join(
  dplyr::count(mouse_cells, mouse, sort, name = "cells"),
  labelled |>
    dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(mouse_cells, cell, mouse), by = "cell") |>
    dplyr::distinct(cell, mouse, tube) |>
    dplyr::mutate(sort = sort_of(tube)) |>
    dplyr::count(mouse, sort, name = "labelled"),
  by = c("mouse", "sort")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(labelled = tidyr::replace_na(labelled, 0L),
                `rate` = sprintf("%.3f%%", 100 * labelled / cells)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

B0304 has **92.0%** of its cells in the mCherry⁻ fraction — 20,817 of 22,632 — against 33.7% for
B0301 and 35.6% for B0303. Divide by that and the picture changes completely. (The figures below are
counted over every barcode the demultiplexer called; the table above recounts over this report's
embedding, so the two differ by whatever QC dropped. The ratios are not sensitive to that.)

| mouse | cells, mCherry⁺ | cells, mCherry⁻ | rate, mCherry⁺ | rate, mCherry⁻ | ⁻ as % of ⁺ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B0301 | 18,122 | 9,217 | 0.94% | 0.054% | **5.8%** |
| B0303 | 17,557 | 9,724 | 3.74% | 0.103% | **2.7%** |
| B0304 | 1,815 | 20,817 | 7.93% | 0.130% | **1.6%** |

The per-cell detection rate in the mCherry⁻ fraction spans 0.054% to 0.130% — a factor of 2.4, not
70 — and measured against each mouse's *own* mCherry⁺ rate, B0304 leaks the **least** of the three.
The earlier conclusion is withdrawn in both of its versions: it is not B0301 and it is not B0304.

This is the second time in this report that a composition has been mistaken for a rate, the first
being the labelled-cell denominator in the co-occurrence test. Both times the error produced a
large, clean-looking number pointing at a real-sounding conclusion. The guard is mechanical: **never
divide labelled cells by labelled cells.**

**What is left, and it is the more interesting finding.** B0304's cells are 92% mCherry⁻ while the
other two mice are near a third, and its mCherry⁺ cells carry the highest detection rate of any
mouse at 7.93%. That is a statement about the animal — engraftment, sorting, or vector expression —
and not about any integration site. It is the same phenomenon as the IS05 question below, in the
same mouse, and the two should be treated as one open item.

**IS10 follows from that, and nothing should be read into its mCherry⁻ fraction.** IS10 is a B0304
clone — 87 of 87 singlet-called cells — and its 26% mCherry⁻ fraction is its mouse's sorting
composition, not a property of the locus. Per cell it runs at 0.125% in the negative fraction
against 4.02% in the positive, a ratio of 3.1% against B0304's 1.6% overall: the same order, nothing
anomalous. **No silencing or position-effect claim should be built on IS10.**

**The 5′ channel advertises a 10 bp floor it does not have.** `classify_five_prime_clips()` sorts
5′ clips into a discovery tier at `min_discovery` (25 bp) and an assignment tier at `min_assign`
(10 bp), but only the discovery tier is ever written: `write_clip_fasta(five, "discovery", …)`. The
assignment tier is computed, counted in the waterfall, and then dropped. `five_prime.fa` contains no
clip shorter than 25 bases, which confirms it. This is the same family as `-T 30` and `-T 12` — a
threshold that reads as active and is not — except that here nothing silently discards the reads
downstream; they are never sent downstream at all.

The gain being left on the table is real but modest: those clips could be matched against the
mini-reference by the same exact positional test the 3′ assignment tier uses, since the flanks are
cut ±200 bp around the 3′ junction and so contain the 5′ junction four bases away. It is a design
change rather than a fix, so it is recorded rather than made. Note also that the 5′ discovery clips
that *are* sent place poorly — 44% of the 25–34 bp band reaches MAPQ ≥ 30, 54% of 35–49 — so this
channel sits in the same MAPQ-0 blind spot as the 3′ one.

**The 20 bp clustering window is not hiding junction-base scatter.** Reads are merged into sites
within `cluster_window = 20`, which could in principle absorb a spread of nearby junction positions
into one call and make a fuzzy site look exact. It does not: of the 1,396 genome-mapped reads that
fall inside a called site, **every one sits at offset exactly 0** from that site's junction base — one
distinct position per site, at every one. The window could be set to 1 and nothing in this channel
would change. Integration is a point event and these reads resolve it to the base.

**Clip length biases which loci are findable, and that bias is now measured rather than asserted.** A
junction whose flanking host sequence is repetitive yields clips that align at MAPQ 0 and is silently
lost: 86 of 974 discovery clips (8.8%) sit at MAPQ 0. IS10 is what that was hiding — a 99-cell clone
whose three 3′ clips end on the junction base exactly and are all unplaceable. The genome-mapped
channel largely repairs this, because 120–140 bases of host place where 44 do not, which is why it
finds four sites the 3′ channel cannot and misses none that it can. What remains is that sites are
still enriched for integrations into sequence unique *at 130 bp* — which is also where genes are,
partly confounding the intragenic enrichment used above as a sanity check.

**A replicate's absence from a compartment may be sampling, not biology.** B0304 contributes 1,399
cells to Rx_4 but only **108** to Rx_6 after QC (1,614 and 201 before it — the counts in the
leakage table above are pre-QC, and the argument here uses the post-QC ones because the detection
rate it multiplies is also post-QC). At IS05's detection rate in Rx_4 (2.64%) that predicts ≈2.9
labelled cells in Rx_6 against 0 observed, *p* ≈ 0.055 — so the apparent "IS05 is HSC-only" pattern is
not supported, and no lineage claim should be built on it. The same caution now has a second
instance: IS05 is one of six B0304 sites rather than that animal's only clone, and IS10, IS11, IS12,
IS14 and IS15 are all sampled from the 1,815 mCherry⁺ cells B0304 contributes against 17,557 for
B0303. **Every B0304 result in this report rests on a tenth of the cells the other animals supply.** B0302 likewise has only 215 cells in Rx_4,
so its zero labelled cells bound within-tube ambient only weakly (<~1.4%), far less tightly than the
empty-droplet measurement above. B0304's hashtag-to-animal mapping used to be the one that could not be
cross-checked by shared clones between compartments, because its only clone was the one missing from
MNC. IS10 closes that: it carries 69 cells in Rx_4 and 4 in Rx_6, so B0304 now has a clone on both
sides of the compartment split.

Even with more cells, RNA could not settle it. If the IS05 provirus sits in a locus that
heterochromatinises on differentiation, the promoter silences, read-through stops, and this pattern
appears with no lineage difference at all — and a silenced provirus is equally absent from the
mCherry⁻ tube. Only DNA distinguishes the two: a bulk integration-site assay on sorted mature B0304
cells, asking whether the IS05 junction is present in genomic DNA. Present in DNA and absent in RNA
means silencing; absent in DNA means genuinely no mature output.

**The ~50 bp clip edge is real but unexplained.** Both channels taper off sharply above ~50 bp of
clipped sequence, with maxima of 62 (host clip) and 69 (vector clip). It is *not*
`outFilterMatchNminOverLread`: chr19 alone holds 30,889 reads of exactly 150 bp with clips ≥ 60 and
matched fractions down to 30–39%, so no 0.66 filter is in force. The implied gap is roughly 70–87
bases of anchor. The reads are absent rather than mis-placed — every read overlapping a junction is
MAPQ 255 with no supplementary, secondary or low-MAPQ population, on both plus- and minus-strand
sites — so there is no hidden yield there, but the cause is not established.

**These reads are counted as host-gene expression — at four sites, and the rule for
which is exact.** A genome-mapped junction read is an ordinary alignment to the host gene as far as
Cell Ranger is concerned: it carries `GN:Z:<host gene>` and `xf:i:25`, and bit 8 of `xf` is the flag
that makes a read a UMI count. So for an affected site the carrying cells gain host-gene UMIs that
are really vector transcript, in exactly the cells a cis-effect test would compare.

It needs **two** conditions, and the second keeps it off most sites. The read has to land inside the
gene, and it has to be in the gene's own orientation — an antisense read is tagged with the gene but
not counted. An earlier draft of this paragraph cited "177 spurious *Ddx10* UMIs in Rx_4"; that was
wrong, because IS02's provirus is antisense to *Ddx10* and none of those reads is counted. The
prediction was tested against the count matrix at six sites and it holds at all six:

| site | host gene | orientation | junction share of carriers' host-gene UMIs |
|---|---|---|---|
| IS10 | *Gm35330* | same sense | **23.5%** |
| IS04 | *Abhd17c* | same sense | **20.9%** |
| IS11 | *Stau2* | same sense | **12.1%** |
| IS03 | *Hells* | same sense | 2.3% |
| IS02 | *Ddx10* | antisense | 0.4% |
| IS01 | *Mef2c* | antisense | 0.0% |
| IS09 | *Fnbp1* | antisense | 0.0% |

`integration_sites.csv` carries this as `cis_confound`, true for **IS03, IS04, IS10 and IS11**. For
those four, any cis-effect test must drop UMIs whose reads contain the provirus terminus before
comparing anything; for the other eleven the question does not arise. IS03's share is small only
because *Hells* is highly expressed, not because the mechanism is weaker there.

**What this measurement is not.** Carrying cells do show more host-gene signal than other cells —
2.5× for *Hells*, 4.0× for *Stau2* — and removing the junction UMIs does not remove that. It is not
evidence of a cis-effect either, because "other cells" here is every other cell in the tube, which
mixes cell type with clone identity: a clone is a lineage, and its host gene may simply be a gene
that lineage expresses. The confound is now quantified and removable; the cis-effect question is
untouched and needs a matched comparison.
